body.x: M&G ENT. (CEO Seong-Joo Ahn, www.twokey.co.kr) unveiled its Windows and Android dual booting tablet, "Twokey Pro," and its wireless video transmission device, "Twokey Mirroring," at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.
The Twokey Pro is the world’s first Windows and Android, dual-booting, tablet PC. It comes fitted with a CPU (I5/Celeron/Atom) and users can choose between a 2~4G RAM and 64~256 SSD.

The device has a 11.6” HD LED Display as well as a front and back dual camera. Consumers have the option to purchase a USB magnetic docking keyboard. The Twokey Pro comes with a digitizer pen and interactive solution program and the tablet PC’s low heat emission and long battery usage are just some of the product’s strengths.

The Twokey Pro has a light touch display that makes use of a wide variety of mouse functions while its shortcuts menu button allows the user to easily adjust the display’s brightness, Wi-Fi, Blutooth, camera, and other functions.

"Twokey Mirroring" is a mirroring device compatible with any device and OS that supports HDMI. It allows high quality video and audio files from a laptop, tablet PC, smart phone, and other devices to be wirelessly transmitted to a TV, projector, or other large-size screen. Potential connectivity and static issues have been greatly reduced and it doesn’t require the installation of any hardware or software for its use. Wireless transmission at 1080P 60 Hz can be done up to 30m and it supports special functions such as N:1, 3D, HID, and more.

M&G ENT., began in 2005 and successfully commercialized the world’s first dual booting tablet PC, the Twokey series. It has since developed the wireless video transmission device (Twokey Mirroring), interactive education solution program (Twokey ES), and other smart education and IT products.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
